events.title: Lafayette Gilchrist ft. Cecil Brooks of the Sun Ra Arkestra
events.description:
$25 at the door / $20 in advance / $15 students and seniors / 7:30 doors / seated 
 
 
 
 
    Get Tickets
   
 
 
 
 
 
 Lafayette Gilchrist featuring special guest and Cambridge native, Cecil Brooks of the Sun Ra Arkestra. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Lafayette Gilchrist’s music draws on the span of jazz history from stride to free improvisation, along with inspiration from hip-hop, funk, and Washington D.C.’s unique go-go sound. His work thrives on making surprising connections between styles and influences, boldly veering from piledriver funk to piquant stride, vigorous swing to hip-hop swagger, contemplative abstraction to deep-bottom grooves. Gilchrist is the pianist in the Sun Ra Arkestra, has toured extensively with David Murray, and his compositions have graced the soundtracks of David Simon’s acclaimed series The Wire, The Deuce, and Treme. Gilchrist has performed with Cassandra Wilson, Macy Gray, Oliver Lake, Andrew Cyrille, Orrin Evans, Paul Dunmall, Hamid Drake, William Parker and many more. Gilchrist’s second solo recording, 2019 “Dark Matter” which muses on the elusive and mysterious matter that ties the universe together, landed on numerous critics best of lists. events.title: UPSTAIRS: Somerville Songwriter Sessions
events.description:
Learn more / Buy Tickets
   
 
 
 
 
 As it has for more than a decade, Somerville Songwriter Sessions presents the finest acoustic singer-songwriters each month in an intimate, welcoming setting. Each concert features three songwriters each doing a solo set, and then trading songs in the round, allowing for stories, impromptu harmonies, jamming, and spontaneous inspiration. Each show, one of our five hosts – Rachel Marie, Terry Kitchen, Sam Bayer, Beth DeSombre, Jack Byrne – are joined by some of the best local and touring singer-songwriters on the scene. November 8: Rachel Marie Rachel Marie (she/they) follows in a tradition of unapologetically forthright femme folksingers, with songs that hearken to "overstuffed lines of Tori Amos, philosophical turn of Indigo Girls, and lilting vocals like Joni Mitchell" (Victoria Farmer, The Christian Humanist Podcast). The social awareness of folk meets the introspection and healing of the singer-songwriter tradition, featuring the emotional catharsis and dynamic vocals of a Broadway show. With a songwriting approach as raw and honest as it's always been, Rachel Marie is making a return to live performance after an unintentional hibernation hiatus, ready to reconnect with a real live audience. December 13: Beth DeSombre Beth DeSombre writes songs that are "smart and  uplifting...focusing on the quiet meaning to be found in ordinary life" (Sing Out! Magazine), exploring issues from the personal to the political. Her music touches both mind and heart, with insights wrapped in melody and harmony that stay with you after the echoes of the last chorus have faded away. Her newest CD Holding the Threads (2024) is her most personal album to date, telling stories about family and crisis and trying to find hope in dark times. Her previous EP The Sea Beside Us (2023), tells stories of ships and the ocean. Her 2017 EP Resistance, which was written in response to the political situation after the 2016 election, is a fundraiser for the ACLU. An award-winning writer in many formats, she has published 8 books. $15 in advance. (+ processing fees) $20 at the door. This Is An All Ages Show Doors are at 3:30pm. Showtime is 4pm. Dinner and drinks available at all tables. NO REFUNDS OR EXCHANGES

A Boston area singer/guitarist, Chuck primarily performs solo but also plays out with his band, The Butler Frogs. He has opened for touring bands America, The Wallflowers, and The Gin Blossoms. In 2020, The Butler Frogs released their sole EP, Last Call For Opinions.

He was also a founding member of Northern Point (2005-2010), an acoustic trio from the NY/NJ area that released three albums (November, Northern Point: Live at St. James' Gate, and After The Frost). 

In 2016, Chuck founded and hosted (with musician Ronnie Hirschberg) the award-winning podcast Above The Basement - Boston Music and Conversation, which won a 202o Boston Music Award for Podcast/Radio Show of the Year.  After 200 episodes, Chuck shuttered the podcast and set out on his solo musical endeavor. 

 He currently performs in New England and is always on the lookout for the lost songs that have influenced him over the years.

events.title: Toad Sunday Revival - The Dennis Brennan Band
events.description: Dennis Brennan was born on the wrong side of the tracks in Marlboro, Massachusetts. At age 9 he entered show business as Rumplestiltsken in a grammar school play. In 7th grade he performed “Louie Louie” with a local garage band at the Berlin, Ma. Town Hall and quickly evolved into “the lead singer” That band evolved into “The Paranoids”, his musical outlet throughout his high school years. They opened shows for both The Remains and The Barbarians, garage band legends who are each featured on “Nuggets, original artyfacts from the first psychedelic era” Rhino R2 75486. Following high school. Brennan’s education continued as lead singer in such well regarded outfits as “The Dirty Rye Band”, The West Side Band”, “The Martells”, and “Push Push”. These bands performed in every bar and dive on the east coast. An education indeed. In 1992 he formed the Dennis Brennan Band and started his solo career, quickly releasing two critically acclaimed recordings on Upstart Records, a division of Rounder. In 2000 he released “Rule #1” on ESCA Records which resulted in glowing reviews from The New Yorker, The Chicago Sun Times, The Boston Phoenix as well as other publications nationwide. These recordings showcase Brennans ability “to not just tip toes into genres, he strips naked and plunges right in.” Bill Holmes, AMPLIFIER.

events.title: Toad Sunday Revival - Tim Gearan Band
events.description: A beloved fixture in the Boston music scene for over 25 years, Tim Gearan has become a bonafide local music hero. His warm, raspy baritone, jaw-dropping guitar skills and wry, poignant songwriting have graced the bars, pubs, and music halls throughout New England and beyond, creating a loyal cult-like following. Gearan, a New York native, spent ten years touring the globe as a sideman for the great Toni Lynn Washington, as well as collaborating with Grammy-winning singer/guitarist Susan Tedeschi. Finding his own artistic voice, Gearan  has crafted an intoxicating blend of Americana, folk and blues with shades of Randy Newman, Tom Waits, JJ Cale,  Leon Russell and Lowell George. He quickly established himself as a force in the Boston’s resurgent roots music scene, and his Boston area residencies have become a “can’t miss” staple of the city’s nightlife. Gearan has released 7 albums to date, as well as 4 single releases; “While the World Goes By” (2019)  “It’s Not the End of the World"  (2019) “Hey, Hey, Hey” (2020) and “Talk About Heaven” (2020).

events.title: UPSTAIRS: Somerville Songwriter Sessions
events.description:
Learn more / Buy Tickets
   
 
 
 
 
 As it has for more than a decade, Somerville Songwriter Sessions presents the finest acoustic singer-songwriters each month in an intimate, welcoming setting. Each concert features three songwriters each doing a solo set, and then trading songs in the round, allowing for stories, impromptu harmonies, jamming, and spontaneous inspiration. Each show, one of our five hosts – Rachel Marie, Terry Kitchen, Sam Bayer, Beth DeSombre, Jack Byrne – are joined by some of the best local and touring singer-songwriters on the scene. December 13: Beth DeSombre Beth DeSombre writes songs that are "smart and  uplifting...focusing on the quiet meaning to be found in ordinary life" (Sing Out! Magazine), exploring issues from the personal to the political. Her music touches both mind and heart, with insights wrapped in melody and harmony that stay with you after the echoes of the last chorus have faded away. Her newest CD Holding the Threads (2024) is her most personal album to date, telling stories about family and crisis and trying to find hope in dark times. Her previous EP The Sea Beside Us (2023), tells stories of ships and the ocean. Her 2017 EP Resistance, which was written in response to the political situation after the 2016 election, is a fundraiser for the ACLU. An award-winning writer in many formats, she has published 8 books. $15 in advance. (+ processing fees) $20 at the door. This Is An All Ages Show Doors are at 3:30pm. Showtime is 4pm. Dinner and drinks available at all tables. NO REFUNDS OR EXCHANGES

events.title: Toad Sunday Revival - The Dennis Brennan Band
events.description: Dennis Brennan was born on the wrong side of the tracks in Marlboro, Massachusetts. At age 9 he entered show business as Rumplestiltsken in a grammar school play. In 7th grade he performed “Louie Louie” with a local garage band at the Berlin, Ma. Town Hall and quickly evolved into “the lead singer” That band evolved into “The Paranoids”, his musical outlet throughout his high school years. They opened shows for both The Remains and The Barbarians, garage band legends who are each featured on “Nuggets, original artyfacts from the first psychedelic era” Rhino R2 75486. Following high school. Brennan’s education continued as lead singer in such well regarded outfits as “The Dirty Rye Band”, The West Side Band”, “The Martells”, and “Push Push”. These bands performed in every bar and dive on the east coast. An education indeed. In 1992 he formed the Dennis Brennan Band and started his solo career, quickly releasing two critically acclaimed recordings on Upstart Records, a division of Rounder. In 2000 he released “Rule #1” on ESCA Records which resulted in glowing reviews from The New Yorker, The Chicago Sun Times, The Boston Phoenix as well as other publications nationwide. These recordings showcase Brennans ability “to not just tip toes into genres, he strips naked and plunges right in.” Bill Holmes, AMPLIFIER.

events.description:
Founded in 2022 by Sapphire Skye Toth and Michael Gehman while they earned their Master of Science degrees in Arts Administration at Boston University, Orkest is meant to be the place where New Music meets The Community and The Community meets New Music.

Orkest, a visionary musical venture rooted in the bustling city of Boston, is on a mission to redefine the local music scene. Recognizing the abundance of untapped musical talent, Orkest seeks to bridge the gap between emerging composers and the community, breaking away from classical traditions and creating an inviting space for diverse genres. Departing from conventional models, Orkest utilizes venues to bring people to music, not just vice versa, fostering a casual environment in cafe bars and libraries. With a commitment to equitable treatment of artists, creating opportunities for artists at socioeconomic disadvantages, professional recordings of performances, and a unique pay-what-you-wish model, Orkest is not just a music experience; it's a transformative force shaping how communities engage with and appreciate new music and the artists who create it.

compositions that blend Congolese rumba and contemporary seben guitar 
styles with other African musics and Western styles like shoegaze, surf,
 and dub. The group is led by guitarist Nathaniel Braddock. Braddock has
 traveled extensively in West and Central Africa, and collaborated with 
many musicians from Ghana, Congo, Zambia, Uganda, Mali, Mozambique, and 
Senegal, as well as US and Australian Indie rock bands. He
 is joined by Ugandan bassist Alex Donsal Kateregga and drummer Frank 
Aveni. The group gets compared to vibey instrumental guitar trios Khruangbin and La Lom,but with more notes.

Sean Patton
 is a comedian based in New York, by way of New Orleans.  (2010), 
Conan
 (2011, 2013), and Comedy Central’s 
The Half Hour 
(2013). More recently, He's been on 
@midnight
 (2014, 2015), 
The Meltdown with Jonah and Kumail 
(2015), 
This Is Not Happening
 (2015, 2017, 2019), Showtime's 
Live from SXSW 
(2017), TruTv's 
Comedy Knockout
 (2016, 2017, 2018), and 
This week at the Comedy Cellar

Scuttlebutt",

Number One

Comedy Central's 
Inside Amy Schumer, 
and TruTV's 
Those Who Can't. 
He stars alongside Brian Jordan Alvarez, Stephanie Koenig, Enrico Colantoni, and Carmen Christopher in two seasons of FX’s 
English Teacher

past_events.title: Bruce Gertz Quintet
past_events.description:
$15 / $10 students / 7pm doors / 7:30 start / seated Bruce Gerts, bass Rick DiMuzio, tenor sax Gilson Schachnik, piano Gary Fieldman, drums 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Bruce's new solo recordings are like meditations that vibrate in the solar plexus and resonate through your being. His command of the instrument and imagination are an elixir for being transported to the pure music channel. Bravo Bruce -  Jerry Bergonzi Every morning, world-renowned jazz bassist, composer, and educator, Bruce Gertz, makes himself a cup of coffee and sits at the baby grand piano of his Melrose, MA living room. Surrounded by quirky plants, records of his esteemed inspirations, and albums of his own, Gertz composes something every day, regardless of the day’s events ahead. He says, "Sometimes I only get a short idea but that can be the seed of a beautiful composition." His counterparts applaud him for his restless commitment to self-improvement. Gertz is known for his superb mastery of the upright bass and was named “Outstanding Bassist” by Boston Music Awards. What some fans don’t know is that he grew up playing electric bass from the age of 14 and still plays (and teaches) the electric quite often. His extraordinary contribution to music education has earned him multiple recognition awards from The International Association of Jazz Educators and the Jazz Education Network. He has been serving as a Professor of Bass at Berklee College of Music since 1976. Additional educator credits include serving on the advisory board of the International Society of Bassists and as an adjudicator at the Clark Terry UNH Jazzer's Festival. Gertz has performed and recorded with such artists as Gary Burton, Jerry Bergonzi, John Abercrombie, Joey Calderazzo, Kenny Werner, Mick Goodrick, Kurt Rosenwinkel, Billy Hart, Bill Frisell, Bob Berg, George Cables, Gil Evans, Tom Harrell, Jon Hendricks, Diane Schuur, Dave Brubeck, George Garzone, Mike Stern, Larry Coryell, Joe Lovano, Cab Calloway, Maynard Ferguson, Count Basie and many others. He is an author of six books and contributing editor to Bass World Magazine. As a bandleader, Gertz has recorded more than twenty albums. His latest quartet release received four stars in Downbeat, December, 2017.

past_events.title: Speed Dating Ages 50+ in Malden, MA at Idle Hands Craft Ales
past_events.description: Reserve your spot here Ready to meet local singles face-to-face? Join us for a fun, low-pressure evening of meaningful connections! Ditch the swiping. Come meet real, local singles in person. This is your excuse to get out, look good, grab a drink, and actually connect with people face to face. No more endless texting and never meeting in-person, no more guessing.. just a fun, social night where you can talk, laugh, flirt, and see what happens. Our speed dating events are designed to feel natural and effortless. It’s everything you wish dating apps felt like… but in real life. Note on Age Range:  While this event is geared toward the age range listed in the title, it’s not a strict rule. If you feel like you’d vibe with this crowd, you’re welcome to join. Our goal is always to create a well-balanced group where connections actually make sense. 🎟️ Ticket Pricing Reserve your spot early! Ticket prices increase once the first 20 tickets have been sold. Our events are intentionally kept at a comfortable size to ensure everyone has enough time to meet each participant. As events fill up, ticket prices increase, so we recommend reserving your spot early to lock in the best price. Don’t wait. Secure your ticket before the first 20 spots are gone! ⸻ How the Night Works Start with a Social Mixer Kick things off with a relaxed mingle. Grab a drink (not included, but highly encouraged), settle in, and get comfortable before the rounds begin. Easy, Guided Conversations We keep things flowing so you don’t have to overthink it. Each round includes a fun icebreaker, and our host guides the room so everything feels smooth, upbeat, and never awkward. Quick, Real Connections You’ll spend a few minutes with each person, just enough time to catch a vibe before rotating. It’s light, fun, and way more natural than sitting through a full date. Match the Ones You’re Into After each round, you’ll mark “friend,” “date,” or “none” on our simple matching system. If it’s mutual, we’ll send you each other’s info the next day. ⸻ A Few Things to Know ⏰ Please arrive 15–30 minutes early to check in and get settled. We start on time, and late arrivals may not be accommodated. 💡 This is meant to be fun! The best way to enjoy it is to stay open, be present, and focus on meeting new people. Some people leave with a match, others leave with new connections—either way, it’s a great night.

Join The West End Museum for a walking tour of the Big Dig’s triumphs and tribulations from the Central Artery to the Rose Kennedy Greenway.    The Big Dig was an ambitious project, an engineering marvel, and a complicated solution to a complicated problem. From burying a highway under an active city to building the world’s first asymmetrical cable-stayed bridge, this tour will uncover how the Central Artery Project left its mark on Downtown Boston and beyond. past_events.title: UPSTAIRS: Macdara Yeates Concert
past_events.description:
Learn more / Buy Tickets
   
 
 
 
 
 Thursday August 27, 7pm McCarthy’s Pub Upstairs, 1920 Massachusetts Ave, Cambridge, MA (Right on Porter square) $20 for FSSGB members, $25 for non-members Macdara Yeates  is an Irish folk singer. Born and raised in Dublin, Yeates is one of a crop of artists associated with the recent resurgence of young folk talent in the Irish capital, alongside acts such as Lankum, Ye Vagabonds, and Landless. In 2012, Macdara became a founding member of The Night Before Larry Got Stretched, a monthly Dublin folk gathering, counting such luminaries as Lisa O’Neill, Ian Lynch and Radie Peat (Lankum) among its earliest attendees. Then, from 2013 to 2017, Yeates served as a member of seven-piece trad ensemble Skipper’s Alley, recording and touring across the UK, Europe, India, Canada, and the USA. Following the release of  Traditional Singing from Dublin , Macdara was nominated for two RTÉ Radio One Folk Awards, including a nomination for ‘Best Folk Singer’ alongside Ríognach Connolly, Cathy Joran and Christy Moore. With a stentorian voice described as “a bracing, baleful, baritone that sounds as if it’s been dug from the deepest, most fragrant turf” (Songlines), Macdara Yeates is ploughing his furrow as a solo performer, garnering wide critical praise and performing on some of the most coveted stages in folk music, from An Góilín Traditional Singers’ Circle to the Sidmouth Folk Festival. “Macdara Yeates is a mighty chanter.” – Christy Moore “In a golden age for traditional singing in Ireland, Yeates’s debut comes as a further welcome affirmation that the torch is being passed to a generation who truly understand and value its worth, while unafraid to inhabit it with their own particular voice.” – The Irish Times

past_events.description:
18+ w/ 2-Item Suggested Minimum. Please Arrive Early to Guarantee Seating.




Geneva Rust-Orta
 is a comic and writer originally from Oakland, CA. She was named Second Funniest Jew at the 2015 Jewish Comedian of the Year Festival in London, UK. She took a half-hour comedy show to the Edinburgh Fringe Festival in 2016 and 2017 and performed another half-hour, "Gayby Girl", off-Broadway at the SoHo Playhouse in 2022 and 2023. Currently based in Brooklyn, she is a regular at the SoHo Playhouse Huron Comedy Club and was titled "Resident Sex Symbol" at Cuckoo's Open Mic. Originally from the Bay, she's performed in the Oakland Comedy Festival, Santa Cruz Comedy Festival, and SF Sketchfest.




Gabbie Watts
 is a stand-up comic based in Atlanta, GA. She’s a regular at the Laughing Skull Lounge and has brought her aggressive monotone and wry charm to Lookout Comedy Festival, Red Clay Comedy Festival, West End Comedy Fest, Flyover Comedy Festival, and Fountain City Comedy Festival. She was the winner of the 2023 “Queer of the Year” competition at the P3 Comedy Fest. Also a history buff, Gabbie hosts iHeart podcast American Filth, where she tells a filthy story from American history every week through a bisexual revisionist lens. Her comedy songs are beloved by hordes of mentally ill adults on TikTok.

past_events.title: Benedict Koh x Caleb Schmale x Charlie Watson x Noah Mark / durianhead
past_events.description: $10 cover / 10pm doors / 10:15 start / all ages durianhead and Benedict Koh's quartet will be offering up an evening of avant-garde music across a dizzying array of genres and performance practices. With an all-star cast from NEC, Benedict Koh's quartet offers up a freewheeling, introspective set of free improvisation and avant-garde jazz; while durianhead's set of experimental laptop electronics weaves IDM, glitch, noise, plunderphonics, footwork and more into a singular 40min set. durianhead is a Boston-based Singaporean musician working with noise, glitch, ambient, drone and experimental electronics. Using self-made digital instruments, they explore the increasingly blurred lines between accessible and avant-garde; a singular and egalitarian third-stream voice wrangling every last bit of sonic detritus into monolithic walls of sound, color and light. a confluence of tangled, twisting lines by durianhead Benedict Koh x Caleb Schmale x Charlie Watson x Noah Mark: Benedict Koh (bass), Caleb Schmale (saxophone), Charlie Watson (trumpet) and Noah Mark (drums) form a quartet of NEC students that work within free improvisation and avant-garde jazz idioms. past_events.title: Hatha Yoga w/ Live Music
past_events.description:
$20-$25 at the door / $15 students & seniors / 12pm start  Experience the magic of a moving meditation with Integral Yoga instructor Vienna-Parashakti. This 90-minute class is appropriate for all students, from beginners to advanced yogis. Dress comfortably, and bring a cozy blanket if you’d like. 
 
 
 
 
    Reserve a spot
   
 
 
 
 
 
 (cash or venmo accepted at the door) 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Prepare to relax and rejuvenate your body, mind, and spirit in this peaceful yoga class. Explore the guided practice of Hatha Yoga and experience a series of classical Yoga asanas (physical postures), pranayama (breath control), Yoga Nidra (deep relaxation) and meditation.  
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Parashakti  (Vienna) is an Integral Yoga instructor and a new-ish resident to Cambridge from two and a half years studying and teaching at  Satchidananda Ashram  in Yogaville, Virginia.  She is currently teaching weekly Hatha Yoga classes at the Lilypad and other places around Cambridge. 
 
 
 
 
 
 Musical accompaniment on the Grand Piano provided by Jesse Gallagher, along with selections from his meditation album "The Inner Sound." 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 “ It was such a delight to attend your class.  My nervous system has been a wreck and it was wonderful to be in a place that felt safe for my body.  I haven’t moved my “yogi” body in years and it felt so good to wake up the cobwebs. Thank you for providing such a beautiful space for me in a day that I really needed it. ” 
 
 — Maria 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Yoga Classes at Lilypad continue weekly on Saturdays.

From burying a highway under an active city to building the world’s first asymmetrical cable-stayed bridge, this tour will uncover how the Central Artery Project left its mark on Downtown Boston and beyond.    Walk the streets of the West End and trace the path of Boston’s biggest urban planning project from the old central artery to the Rose Kennedy Greenway.    Tours begin at the West End Museum. past_events.title: Psychedelic Soundbath w/ Jesse Gallagher
past_events.description:
$25 general admission / $15 students & seniors / 7:30 doors / 8pm start / lying down & seated Relax into a psychedelic world of color and sound in this Soundbath with Jesse Gallagher. Space is limited! 
 
 
 
 
    Get Tickets
   
 
 
 
 
 
 Jesse fills the Lilypad with a live ambient soundbath along with his colorful analog projections making Lilypad’s muraled walls come to life! This show is best enjoyed lying down on a yoga mat, making yourself as comfortable as possible. Please bring a pillow, blanket, slippers or anything else to make this experience cozy. Yoga mats will be provided. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Jesse Gallagher  began living above the Lilypad in 2006, just a few blocks from where his grandfather grew up on Inman St.  At the time, Jesse was in the middle of what would be about a decade of regular touring, performing & recording with his psychedelic rock band Apollo Sunshine.  The band was featured in the New York Times, Rolling Stone, Spin & shared the stage with legendary acts  Wu-Tang Clan ,  Toots & The Maytals ,  The Flaming Lips  &  Dr. Dog . Jesse has been involved with the Lilypad for 20 years and the full time talent booking agent since 2013. Breaking Bad used Jesse’s song “We are Born When We Die” (2008) to dramatic effect. “Today is the Day” (2005) was in international Nike commercials while his ballad “Singing to the Earth to Thank Her For You” was used in a large GAP campaign. Gallagher has collaborated, recorded & performed extensively w/  Sam Cohen ,  Willy Mason ,  Lilys ,  Nick Nicely ,  Doug Tuttle  &  Edan . Gallagher is a certified Yoga & Meditation teacher and hosts classes at the Lilypad & online. Since 2018, he has released 40 pieces of instrumental music which have been used in millions of YouTube videos ranging from NBC NY to Tesla and most recently a string of viral videos by Emma Chamberlain. Gallagher has a very active YouTube channel, making lots of psychedelic music videos and building a community of mindful listeners. @jessegallagher.tv
